title: One Agreement to a Site: How Many Micro Markets a Client May Hold
content:
A client of the Unattended Micro Market Program may hold as many micro market agreements as it has sites, and there is no ceiling on the number held at once. Each agreement is written against exactly one site and one kiosk reference, and sales, subsidy funding, shrink and settlement belong to that site's agreement alone.

## The clause

1. A further micro market agreement is not opened for a site that already carries an open micro market agreement. Only 1 open agreement may stand for a site at any time.
2. A site's agreement counts as open while it is proposed, installing, active or suspended, and counts as gone once it is closed, so a site whose earlier market has been removed may take a fresh agreement.
3. Where the client wants a second market on another floor of a site already under agreement, that market is added to the existing agreement as a second kiosk rather than opened as a second agreement.

## Evidence for the judgement

The judgement is made before the new agreement is opened, and it is made on the company's own records rather than on what the client says about the site. The records consulted are the agreements already standing for that client and that site code: the client the agreement is written for, the site code, the standing of the agreement and its reference number. Where such an agreement is found and its standing is proposed, installing, active or suspended, a further agreement for the same site is not opened. Two agreements for the same client and site are distinguished by their start date, their kiosk reference and the market format written on them.

## Hypothetical cases

A client holds an agreement at its warehouse site standing suspended and asks for a micro market at that same site. The suspended agreement counts as open, so no second agreement is opened for the site.

The same client's headquarters site carries an agreement that closed last quarter. A closed agreement counts as gone, so a fresh agreement may be written for that site.

The client then asks for a second market on the fourth floor of the warehouse site. That market is added to the existing agreement as a second kiosk.
